attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. The nearby quotes from Sutskever and Zitron are separate from this sentence.

semantics.note: In context, 'It' means building ever larger LLMs in hopes of reaching AGI. The normalised proposition matches that scope. It is a flat retrospective statement, not a forecast that scaling can never work.

contract.note: Marcus did not define AGI. The plain reading is that no broadly accepted, independently substantiated AGI demonstration came from LLM scaling before 27 Nov 2025. That is the ordinary meaning and does not tilt toward or against him.

evidence.note: ARC Prize's independent testing across labs (June 2025) found every frontier system failed ARC-AGI-2 and concluded new ideas are still needed for AGI. It predates the cutoff. It is one benchmark, but it fits the contract's reading.
The International AI Safety Report's broad assessment (Oct 2025) records persistent gaps on realistic tasks despite big benchmark gains. That fits the absence of a demonstrated AGI before the cutoff.
Google's own Gemini 3 announcement (18 Nov 2025) calls the release a step toward AGI, not AGI itself. It is a company disclosure and works only as a cross-check.

reviews.rationale: On the plain reading, the claim needs no accepted AGI demonstration from LLM scaling by 27 Nov 2025. The independent evaluations in the packet (ARC Prize, International AI Safety Report) show big remaining gaps. The newest frontier release before the cutoff (Gemini 3) was described by Google itself only as a step toward AGI. No counterevidence shows AGI was achieved. The claim is supported.
